newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges "new spirit of community".
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges "new spirit of community".

text.p: President Clinton started his second four-year term as U.S. chief executive on Monday with a call for a "new spirit of community" as the United States enters the 21st century.

"The challenge of our past remains the challenge of our future: will we be one nation, one people, with one common destiny -- or not?" Clinton asked in a speech prepared for delivery at his second inaugural.
Clinton, whose first term was marred by partisan bickering between his Democratic Party and Republicans controlling Congress, said government must change with the times.

"We need a new government for a new century, a government humble enough not to try to solve all our problems for us, but strong enough to give us the tools to solve our problems for ourselves -- a government that is smaller, lives within its means and does more with less," he said.
Echoing the late John Kennedy's theme of a New Frontier, Clinton spoke of "our land of New Promise" where people and government will address problems together.

"There is work to do, work that government cannot do alone. Teaching children to read. Hiring people off welfare. Coming out from behind locked doors and shuttered windows to helpm reclaim our streets from drugs, gangs and crime. Taking time out from our own lives to serve others," he said.

Clinton mentioned international affairs only in passing in his relatively brief address, but vowed that the United States will "stand mighty for peace and freedom and maintain a strong defense against the dark forces of terror and destruction.
